stemBlocks.value: Part (i) of question 8 on this page: the trapezium A on the square grid has vertices (-5, 4), (-4, 4), (-3, 2) and (-5, 2). Draw the image of A after a reflection in the line x = -1 and label this image A'.
Think first: The mirror line x = -1 is vertical, so every point keeps its height and simply flips across to the other side of that line.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p261-q01 from workbook page 261.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read the vertices of trapezium A from the grid.

contentBlocks.value: Two on y = 4 and two on y = 2.

solutionSteps.instruction: Work out the rule for reflecting in the vertical line x = -1.

contentBlocks.value: A point at distance d to the left of x = -1 goes to distance d to the right, so x -> -1 + (-1 - x) = -2 - x, and y is unchanged.

solutionSteps.instruction: Apply the rule to each vertex.
Plot the four image points and join them in the same order to draw A'.

contentBlocks.value: Check: each vertex of A' is the same horizontal distance from x = -1 as its object, on the opposite side.
Result: Trapezium A' drawn to the right of x = -1

strategyBlocks.value: For a reflection in x = -1, the image of (x, y) is (-2 - x, y). Apply this to each vertex of A, then plot and join the images.

whyThisWorks.value: Reflection fixes every point on the mirror line and sends every other point to the point the same perpendicular distance away on the opposite side. Because the mirror x = -1 is vertical, the perpendicular direction is horizontal, so heights are untouched and only x changes. The image is congruent to the object but its orientation is reversed.

commonErrors.misconception: Reflecting in the y-axis and getting (5, 4) instead of (3, 4).
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Reflecting in the y-axis and getting (5, 4) instead of (3, 4).

commonErrors.misconception: Counting the distance to the mirror line from the wrong side.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Counting the distance to the mirror line from the wrong side.

examTip.value: For a reflection in x = a, use x' = 2a - x; for a reflection in y = b, use y' = 2b - y. Test the formula on one vertex by counting squares before trusting it on the rest.
